parameters.content:
## READ BEFORE ACTIVATING

Your n8n ALREADY RUNS a P0.5. This file is a rebuild, not a patch.

**Never leave both Active.** Two workflows writing the same tables is
worse than one.

Safe cutover:
  1. Import this. Leave it INACTIVE.
  2. Fill in Config.
  3. Run it once with the Manual Trigger (or the AD4 Workflows page).
  4. Compare its Summary line against your original's.
  5. Only then: deactivate the original, activate this.

## Endpoint: filled in, NOT reachable from the build machine

`rules_url` is Polymarket's public **Gamma event** lookup by slug:

    https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/events?slug={slug}

`{slug}` is replaced with each open market's `event_slug`.

### Why this job exists

The rules text names the station the market settles on. If Polymarket changes
it mid-market - a different airport, a different rounding rule - every
probability the desk has computed for that market is against the wrong
observation, and nothing else would notice. This job stores the text and flags
the change.

It is the least urgent of the four. Run it daily; skip it entirely while you
are getting the first three working.

**Nothing is written unless rules parse.**

### On the first run

Every market will report its rules as CHANGED, because there is nothing stored
to compare against yet. That is expected exactly once. The second run should
report none changed.

## Why rules text is worth a daily job

The rules say WHICH STATION and WHICH SURFACE settles the market. If
Polymarket edits that mid-life, every probability AD4 computed against the
old station is measuring the wrong thing - and nothing else in the system
would notice.

This workflow stamps `rules_changed_at` ONLY when the text actually moves,
so the column answers "when did the terms last change", not "when did we
last poll".

A run that finds a change reports status `attention`, so it stands out on
the AD4 Workflows page and in the P4.1 watchdog.

Find changes:

    select city_key, resolution_date, rules_changed_at
    from markets
    where rules_changed_at > now() - interval '7 days'
    order by rules_changed_at desc;

nodes.name: Save rules
nodes.notes: PATCH, not upsert: this annotates a market P0.2 created and must never create one. An upsert with only the four rules columns fails with 23502 on any schema where markets has a NOT NULL column they do not cover, because ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE checks NOT NULL on the proposed row before it finds the conflict.

parameters.content:
## Why this workflow is capped, and why it forgets

**max_bands_per_run / max_markets_per_run ship with a small number.**
This job makes ONE REQUEST PER ITEM - roughly 800 across 37 cities. A first
Execute with no cap fires 800 sequential requests at Polymarket and either sits
there for an hour or takes the instance down. Raise it once you have seen a run
finish.

**A successful run does not keep its data.** n8n's execution store holds the
input AND output of every node, so a workflow whose job is to move a large
third-party payload into Supabase holds that payload twice and then writes it
into the executions database - on every run. That is what shows up as
"workspace offline, 503".

Failed runs are still saved in full, which is when the payload is worth having.
The Summary node's line is written to `ingest_log` either way, so
`v_workflow_runs` and the AD4 Workflows page still show what happened.
